title: Apply Area Concepts to Solve Problems
objective: I can find the area of a composite figure by decomposing it into basic shapes, including a regular polygon split into triangles, and adding or subtracting the areas.
model: composite figures decomposed into rectangles, triangles and a regular polygon, with pieces added or subtracted

widgets.component: regular octagon sign (base 6 in, height 7 in) and regular hexagon table (base 10 cm, height 9 cm) split into identical center triangles
widgets.root: Challenge §2.7 (octagon, base 6 in, height 7 in) and §5.3 (hexagon, base 10 cm, height 9 cm) give central-triangle heights that no regular polygon has: a regular octagon of side 6 has apothem 7.24 and a regular hexagon of side 10 has apothem 8.66. The numbers are whole-number roundings but the stems do not say 'rounded' (5-9 does say it for every such item), so a student who knows the hexagon is made of equilateral triangles meets a contradiction. The arithmetic of the keys (168, 270) is right for the given numbers.
widgets.replacement: Add the sentence 'The height is rounded to the nearest whole unit, so use the numbers given.' to both stems and the matching explanation, or use exact-by-design values: octagon base 6 in with height 7.2 in (key 8 × ½ × 6 × 7.2 = 172.8 in²) and hexagon base 10 cm with height 8.7 cm (key 6 × ½ × 10 × 8.7 = 261 cm²). Keep the 'splits into identical triangles' wording.
